progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: Chemistry: C1 to C3 (dynamic equilibrium as equal rates; adding a substance speeds up only the reaction that uses it, then the faster rate falls and the slower rate rises until they are equal again; the iron thiocyanate tube; a temperature change speeds up the heat-absorbing reaction more; Le Chatelier's principle). Biology: B10 (co-dominance, roan cattle, 1 : 2 : 1 from two heterozygotes). Year 11: collision theory. Not assumed: any exam-technique vocabulary.
progression.startsWith: An exam question you can answer but might misread. The video opens: Here's something NESA's marking feedback raises every year. In every HSC Chemistry and Biology report from 2020 to 2025, it points out answers that missed what the question actually asked. Often the student knew the science.
progression.stopsAfter: the routine (verb, marks, content words and givens, constraint, then tick each part); the meanings of "in terms of", "with reference to" and "using the information"; "one mark, one idea" with its three limits; two drills.
progression.nextLesson: s02, "Identify, describe, explain: what each verb really asks for".

teaching.task: Before you write a word, what exactly is this question asking for?
teaching.causalExplanation: (1) NESA marking feedback flags answers to a nearby question in every Chemistry and Biology report from 2020 to 2025, so the step before writing matters (1); (2) one HSC-style Chemistry equilibrium question is pulled apart (2); (3) the verb says what to do: explain means show cause and effect (3); (4) the marks say how much to write and when to stop (4); (5) the content words and givens say what the answer is about: ask what each given tells you, then decide if the answer needs it (5); (6) the constraint says how to answer: in terms of, with reference to, using the information (6); (7) the answer is built in collision theory as three linked points (7, 8); (8) a correct Le Chatelier answer still answers a nearby question and loses two marks (9); (9) one mark, one idea is a rule of thumb with three limits (10); the routine and memory aid (11); two drills with feedback (12 to 15); decision rule and handoff (16); key notes (17).
teaching.conversationalApproach: one fact carries the video: every NESA Chemistry and Biology marking feedback report from 2020 to 2025 flags answers to a nearby question. One HSC-style Chemistry equilibrium question is pulled apart one annotation at a time (verb, marks, content words and givens, constraint), the answer is built in the asked terms with a mark counter, and a correct but off-constraint answer shows the cost. Two drills, one per subject, practise the routine.
teaching.openingDecision: Here's something NESA's marking feedback raises every year. In every HSC Chemistry and Biology report from 2020 to 2025, it points out answers that missed what the question actually asked. Often the student knew the science. They just answered a nearby question. So this video is about the step before you write anything: reading the question properly, in about thirty seconds.
teaching.understandingCheck: The narration says "Do the one from your subject, or both". Both drills ask students to run the routine first. Drill 1, Biology: roan cattle data, "using the information provided", explain, 3 marks. It targets the unused-stimulus fault (12/12). Crossed habit: "codominance means both alleles show", with no numbers. Drill 2, Chemistry: N2O4 and NO2 in ice water, "with reference to Le Chatelier's principle", predict and explain, 3 marks. It targets "covers only one requested part" (part of the 12/12 nearby-question fault). Crossed habit: "It goes paler." (predict only). Drill 2 is a temperature change, so it also varies the cause after the worked example's concentration change. Drill 2 deliberately asks for the Le Chatelier answer that the worked example ruled out. Students see the constraint, not the topic, decide the reasoning. Feedback says "this time the constraint asks for Le Chatelier's principle".
teaching.curriculumScope: No syllabus dotpoint (skills video, HSC exam skills series): the NESA glossary of key words (paraphrased) and the Working Scientifically skill Communicating (NSW Chemistry and Biology Stage 6 syllabuses, 2017). starts at "an exam question you can answer but might misread". It stops after the four-part reading routine, the three constraint phrases, the limits of "one mark, one idea" and two practised reads. It does not cover verb meanings in depth (s02), compare and contrast (s03), judgement verbs (s04), calculations (s05), graphs (s06), practicals (s07) or extended responses (s08).

design.visualSystem: Explainer engine: warm paper stage, handwritten Caveat headings, amber doodle layer. The question card is on paper colour. It has a subject badge, the tag "HSC-style question, written for HSCScience", and a printed mark value in brackets at the right, as on HSC papers. The annotation layer on the card: an amber highlighter swipe for the verb; a hand-drawn ring "stamp" round the marks, becoming a marks badge; pen underlines for content words and givens; teal square brackets round the constraint phrase. The answer box is an HSC-booklet-style ruled box (white, faint blue rules, left margin). A mark counter sits in the top-right of the answer box: "0 / 3" ticks to "3 / 3", one per mark-earning point. Each tick lands in the margin beside its line. A label sits under it: "HSCScience marking guide (illustrative)". The routine strip has four rows, each with an icon: highlighter, badge, underline, bracket. It builds in scene 11 and returns as the decision board. Kit: `HandText`, `DrawPath`, `scribbleEllipse`, `Mark`, `Callout`, `Enter`, `Plate`, `Countdown`. The `WrongChip`, `GreyTag` and `Cross` chips are from B6a. No people, hands or faces: the highlighter and pen marks draw themselves. Colours: amber highlighter for verbs; ink pen for underlines; teal brackets for constraints; marker ticks green; lost-mark tags red. No people, hands or faces.
design.transitionPlan: The report-tile grid opens; the question card slides in and straightens; each annotation (highlighter, marks badge, underlines, teal brackets) lands on its cue and adds a routine strip row at the far left; the answer box fills line by line with margin ticks and the mark counter; the weak answer box slides in beside the strong one; the limit cards collapse to their titles as each new one writes; the routine card returns full size, then shrinks; each drill clears the board and its feedback annotates the card before the model answer writes; the decision rule card and next chip close; scene crossfade with settle.
